posts.title: Water filtering
posts.excerpt: Als toelatingsproject voor het HKU ben ik gevraagd om een product te ontwerpen dat een probleem in mijn directe omgeving oplost. Dit gebaseerd op gebeurtenis, wat mij inspireert.. Laat ik eerst even mijn situatie…
posts.content:
Als toelatingsproject voor het HKU ben ik gevraagd om een product te ontwerpen dat een probleem in mijn directe omgeving oplost. Dit gebaseerd op gebeurtenis, wat mij inspireert.. Laat ik eerst even mijn situatie uitleggen, ik ben een tijdje terug gevraagd om op een oude molen te passen.   Hierbij was mijn toewijding om me terug te trekken van de bestaande wereld, en de tijd even stil te laten staan. Zo had ik een houtkacheltje, dat was mijn grote vriend, voor de warmte, maar ook voor het koken, het thee maken, en later zo blijkt, nog wel meer.. Liefst zo energievriendelijk en met zoveel mogelijk mindfulness te leven. Alles was er wel, een knusse bedstee, een keukentje, een werkplaatsje.. en een heerlijke buitenruimte voor als de zon scheen.. verder kon ik mn stroom opwekken met zonnepanelen of windkracht! Het enige wat ik niet had op dit eiland, was een waterbron, dit moest ik elke week met gevulde jerrycans aanvullen.   Dit zette mij aan het denken. Zeker in combinatie met deze opdracht, heb ik mezelf ook opgelegd dat ik voor de oplossing niet het eiland af mag.   Ik heb enorm veel rondgevraagd aan bezoekers op het eiland, sommige hadden wel wat toe te voegen, een persoon in het bijzonder, die wees mij op verschillende technieken voor koolstof productie, en het belangrijkste element, het verwijderen van zuurstof uit het verbrandingsproces. Gebaseerd op de naam Kontiki Kiln, rocket stove en britta filter, heb ik onderzoek gedaan. Kijkend naar de materialen om mij heen, had ik een allesbrander, een mooie kachel om een goed heet vuur in te maken, en een leeg blikje verf, die ik eerst schoon brandde, en vervolgens uitschrobde. Deze heb ik volgestouwd met stukjes hout, die niet boven het oppervlak uit kwamen, en heb alle lege ruimte opgevuld met houtas.   Dus, de noodzakelijke materialen;
  • Een lucifer
  • Een leeg blikje
  • As uit het vuur
  • wat katoen of textiel voor de prop onderin
Verder heb ik gebruikt,
  • Een mooie houtkachel
  • een zeef om de houtskool in te wassen
  • een onderkant van een fles om als trechter te gebruiken
  • een hamer om de houtskool klein mee te maken
      en zie hier het verschil: Het rook niet meer, het was zo helder als de mooiste diamant het was niet gekleurd het smaakte nergens naar   Na het lab resultaat zullen we weten in hoeverre het gelukt is!

posts.title: Concept: an ecologic answer to mosquitos!
posts.excerpt: Set up The idea that bats eat a ton of mosquitoes each night (up to 1200 each HOUR for every adult bat!) I learned their value last summer camping out in a little wood cabin next to three huge lakes in the Pyrenees.…
posts.content:
Set up

The idea that bats eat a ton of mosquitoes each night (up to 1200 each HOUR for every adult bat!) I learned their value last summer camping out in a little wood cabin next to three huge lakes in the Pyrenees. Everybody was swarmed with insects, except around our cabin, which had a rather large colony in the wall. My friend, Max Spruijt, an ecologist, told me he had counted at least 68 individuals. This would surmount to a total of, lets say, 68 * 800(compensation for age) = A monstrous 54400 mosquito's per hour! And trust me, we knew it.. lingering till late with our giant 3 metre doors wide open, and all lights on, i think in the three weeks i was there, i only heard one mosquito, and that buzzing died within seconds, I am guessing the bat Corps saved the day! In comparison, just 400 metres on, and a little uphill, away from the lakes, we where having dinner at friends, and as the night set in, the parasols just became covered in all kinds of insects within seconds. Around our cabin, we only saw all kinds of night dancers, and butterflies. Talking about harmony!

Situation

In modern city planning situations, we are trying to implicate areas for natural habitation by animals. This to propogate an ecology that is sustainable.

Problem

Great as all these implications are, and I really admire them, they do bring some counter effects. Namely, inviting the wildlife into the cities, means inviting them in! So a surplus in rats in Amsterdam West is surely related to the last ten years of ongoing addition of green areas, to make it the greenest neighborhood of Amsterdam, and even of Europe. Also the addition of landing grounds for overflying geese will bring an onset of mosquitos.

Solution

I wish to combat this in the way i learned last summer in the wild. What i want to do is:
  • Survey for mosquito infested neighborhoods
This involves a dramatic campaign, during mosquito season(juli-august) Mosquito's? The solution is near! Batman!!
  • Find sponsorship, either in neighborhood, or in conjunction with council or nature foundations.
  • Scout neighborhood for possible locations
  • Place Bat sensors, to see if the location is good for bats. A self designed microcomputer system that reads the light, temperature and wind at the location during the day for a period of time, and relays this real time to our private servers.
  • Once the locations are chosen, we will use a matrix to decide approx size of colony needed to cover an area, and then design bat homes accordingly.
  The Bat HQ's Basic design is simple, a few lats, some wide planks, and some softish wood for the bats to land upon, thats all that's needed. The basic idea is to emulate a high narrow space, so they can crawl in all the way, and also move down, to where its cooler. This is something they do all by themselves, as they move about to regulate heat. The grooved plank is used as a landing pad, this makes it easier for them to land. Below are examples of the Kent bat box. For printable instructions see bottom of page. These most ingenious designs by Habitat UK really are ingenious, and i hope they will be applied at some point in the future.
Habibat 001 integrated bat box Forticrete bat access brick
    Habibat bat box partnership scheme: enhancing homes for bats
Habibat is a unique partnership between the Bat Conservation Trust,  Ecosurv, Habibats partnership companies and the customer, to provide bat boxes that work for bats and buildings, for more details, please click here.
Making your own box Bats do not like draughts, and prefer well insulated boxes where temperature and humidity remain constant. They also need a rough textured wood to cling to. The wood should not be treated because bats are very sensitive to chemicals. A ‘bat ladder’ or other landing area that leads to an entry slit wide enough to admit bats, but narrow enough to keep out predators is also essential, usually 15 – 20 mm. Once up, a bat box cannot be opened legally without a licence. For more information on bats and the law call the Bat Helpline (0345 1300 228). Things to remember: • Make sure joints are well sealed and avoid large, loose-fitting front panels. • All timber used in bat boxes should be rough sawn (unplaned) and untreated from sustainable sources • Keep entrance slits small (15 -20mm) • Removable lids should not be used and the box should not be opened External ready-made bat boxes  There are a number of ready-made external bat boxes suitable for buildings and trees that can be purchased. These boxes can be wooden as shown above, however there are an increasing number of more durable options, such as Greenwood Ecohabitats ecostyrocrete bat box shown below.

posts.title: Moon Clock
posts.excerpt: Pic: copywrite Elodie Vreeburg So i decided I want to be able to track the moon in the form of a clock. Seen the moon is a regular hardly changing thing, this should be able to be done with just a clock. For added…
posts.content:
Pic: copywrite Elodie Vreeburg So i decided I want to be able to track the moon in the form of a clock. Seen the moon is a regular hardly changing thing, this should be able to be done with just a clock. For added complexity i want to try to implement a WiFi-Module, just so i can make sure it keeps itself in check with the actual moon phase. For the mechanics, there are two main aproaches i have thought of.

2 Dimensional moon-phase clock

First is the 2-dimensional version, where the slices of the moon are divided over a flat surface, and can each individually light up to form a part of the moon. The result would be similar to the picture above, with a somewhat "vectorized" look. This could be handy in places where space is tight, like perhaps a digital pocket-watch.

3Dimensional moon-phase clock

This is my preferred idea, to have a proper wall sized clock, something for in a grand entrance or something similar.   a 3D version would be a much nicer simulation i think, otherwise  it might as well be an app.. on your phone. :) So also the gradient of shadowplay will be much more interesting. The intention will be to make it a soft gradient. ﻿ ​here is a little indicator experiment: ​﻿

posts.content:
Programma van Eisen:

Constructief

  • Schuiven
  • Rondwerk

Oppervlaktebewerking

  • Fineren
  • Decoreren met behulp van lasersnijder
Afwerking
  • Schuren, naar 180
  • Olien
  • Waxen
  • Lakken

Bijzondere verrichtingen

  • Gebruik van CNC (Productie mal voor stoel)
  • Gebruik van eigen gemaakte mal
  • Gebruik van externe experts in hun vakgebied
  Mijn klant, is mijn vader. Hij wil heel graag voor zijn kantoor een mooi set meubels. Hij heeft ook een specifieke wens, en dat is dat hij een ronde tafel wil. Er moet gebruik van gemaakt worden door 8 mensen. Het idee is om het een beetje een spannende en klassieke uitvoering te geven. doch toch modern. In Milaan ben ik een andere versie van deze tafel tegengekomen, en die is me altijd bij gebleven.   https://youtu.be/5sLlJ0PRAZQ?t=13s Deze tafel is ook heel mooi, maar eigenlijk een specialistenproject... wat ik wel kan doen is de vorm van de fineren meenemen. Qua mechanica ben ik voor de tafel rond de 400 euro kwijt, het hout is vooral plaatmateriaal, met een oppervlak van 3m2 en een meerdere tonnen binnenin, kost het multiplex in totaal ook rond de 400 euro. voor de fineerlaag reken ik 200 euro. Ook is er voor het maken van de mallen nog eens 200 euro opzij gelegd. een totaalplaatje qua materialen van 1200,00 euro ex verder zit er behoorlijk wat tijd in, maar omdat het mijn vader is, breng ik deze niet in rekening.   Dan moet er natuurlijk nog een stoeltje bij, en in eerste instantie viel ik voor de mackintosh stijl, vanwege het hoge gehalte aan drama. Maar ik vond ze eigenlijk te lelijk, en te groot, en te oncomfortabel. Ik heb toen verder gekeken bij een persoonlijk van mij, Kishimoto Design.. Ik vind dat het krukje, naast die tafel een prachtige kans zou geven om vakmanschap met massief hout te laten zien. Dit krukje word in princiepe wat ik ga maken. Deze kruk is goedkoper te produceren, vandaar dat ik er hoop meerdere te maken. voor het massief hout ben ik rond de 50 euro per kruk kwijt, plus 10 euro aan lijm, en een verdere investeringskosten voor een mal van mdf, reken ik op 50 euro. plus 75 euro voor leer en touw en gaatjes boren, naaien en patronen maken al met al zou dat voor 4 krukken zijn, 50 + 135*4= 540,00 ex btw.

Haalbaarheid

  De tafel word zeker wat werk, maar in combinatie met een slimmem productiemethode moet dit haalbaar zijn. De pneumatische pompen, zouden wellicht een struikelblok kunnen zijn, maar in princiepe zou dit ook moeten kunnen.      

And then there was #light... And then #therewasnot #butstillwas

posts.excerpt: For school, we needed to make a fancy case for something. My mind went overboard, trying to find a shape nobody else would try. Having recently heard of Frank Chesters "Chestahedron", I had found myself an adequate…
posts.content:
For school, we needed to make a fancy case for something.

My mind went overboard, trying to find a shape nobody else would try.

Having recently heard of Frank Chesters "Chestahedron", I had found myself an adequate challenge.

The Chestahedron, a form known as the first seven sided form with equal surface area.

Its based upon an tetrahedron, that opens up, then forming kites, and stopping at the moment that it becomes of equal surfaces all around.

F. Chester, when he applied for a patent for this shape, he was refused. the grounds being that it was a discovery as opposed to an invention! This making it the youngest of all shapes! since 2005 to be precise.

First up was to draw this shape.

   A small formsketch, to experiment with glueing possibilities.  

Small experiment to get the shape with copper wire.

posts.content:
So last night, a friend showed up at my house with a very special request.

Over the last year or so, I have taken an interest in making plaster casts of people.

My friend knew this, and decided she would love to send her mom a copy of her hand.

Her mom lives far away in Estonia and it's her birthday, so she figured this is the most personal thing she could send.

So we got to work!

 

I am really happy with the end result.

We are very excited to get this sent up.

We are going to get it wrapped up in a big black box and send it by mail.

posts.content: “A Room for Thoughts” is an experimental project that I wish to complete to graduate from my furniture making school. posts.title: Designing a Chair part III
posts.excerpt: With adequate pride, I wish to present my latest design in chair making! 8-2-2016 2320 new flow chair fabric design 8-2-2016 2320 new flow chair with cutout shapes THIS ONE 17-2-2016 new flow chair sq legsfabric A1…
posts.content:
With adequate pride, I wish to present my latest design in chair making!

8-2-2016 2320 new flow chair fabric design 8-2-2016 2320 new flow chair with cutout shapes THIS ONE 17-2-2016 new flow chair sq legsfabric A1 24-03-2016 CABRIOLE POTEN new flow chair

https://sketchfab.com/models/60cc5b2870bb4da1ae04cc420a815cdc

I will keep updating this page as the work process gets along.

http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_N4GawKx9V4

Some parts will prove trial and error, such as the flexibility of the front to the back. I wonder whether it might start 'walking', as the parts bend and flex.

Otherwise I'm excited, as I know it's going to be quite a challenge.

I next step is making the lamination clamps!

Above, you can see a calculation of the amount of springback, when compared to the amount of laminating layers.

So 10 layers divided by, 40mm of displacement = 0.2mm display.

  

With my pressing mold finally working, I stumbled across a major structural issue: that it is actually WAY too flexible...

I have done some basic stress calculations, but think I will need to just experiment most of all.

As you can see, a similar wood birch will flex immensely.

The original 9 mm will flex nearly 9 cm!! But when I brought this up to 15 mm, the sag is way less. My plan is to actually try and switch the grain on some layers.

So this is what I am up to today! :)

Wish me luck :D

UPDATE:

For the next trick, i cross grained my different layers of wood, and in stead of 3 I used 5 layers. Summing up to a total of 15mm instead of 9.

The cross graining is a technique used in Multiplex, to assure plate stability and rigidity.

By starting with a layer that bends in the cross direction and then a layer that bends in the length of the shape, and so on, they both keep each other from bending.

Additionally, I made sure the majority didnt bend in the length, so it looked like,

CROSSGRAIN

LENGTHBEND

CROSSGRAIN

LENGTHBEND

CROSSGRAIN

LENGTHBEND

Looking, and feeling as hard and rigid as a plate of 15 mm multiplex! but then round! :D very pleased with these results.

Now, as the wood process is a working one, i can move on to thinking about the fabric part.

as I have planned, I printed the basic fabric shapes I had designed, and went to work from there.

Now I have my basic fabrics cut and sewed together, I can get to work on the padding, next you see some of my experiments, to get a bit of a feel of what its going to be like.

As it turned out, just one layer of 200gram Dacron fibre was enough to give it that lush puff, but still not too thick for my sewing machine to handle. Consistent results on the stitchlength and tension are as allways with sewing, of dire importance.

Next up, the edging. I wish to run a cord through, to distribute the weight to the ends of the rope.I decided to use fake leather, as it was all my budget at the time would allow for.

after trying several widths and colours, I tried a break test, and it held up quite well, but once it started ripping, there was no hope left.

Not a good quality for a chair. So I made sure it was backed by an extra layer of fabric. Then I sewed it all together.

Giving it some nice padded sewing lines.

And then back to the wood part of the process!

Picked up some gorgeous Elm, Amsterdams most beautiful wood, and set to work making it into nice planks. Then i glued them together as bars of 80x80mm, to work down to a total of 75x75mm.

As is visible throughout my design process, I have been of two minds whenever I thought of the front legs. On the one hand I really liked the heavy front, just huge blocks of legs, in contrast to the springiness of the back legs.

But also I made plans to do the classic cabriole leg, which I sort of left as a thing if i had enough time.

Leaving that to lay for a little longer, i made all the connections in the wood, and drilled a wide hole for the bumbone. (the lower laminated curve)

Back on the home front, I had received my new parts.

Not able to resist, I had to try the parts temporarily with clamps.

what an peculiar shape!

seeing this, I definitely felt the front needed more form-definition, and also a bit more sexyness.

So I decided to roll with the Cabriole Legs!

and also made a basic temporary armrest sketch.

I also considered trying the armrests as blocks.

Very pleased about how the legs curve and feel ready to jump into the air. This binds it in visually with the back.

Also seeing this, I realized blocks wont do, and as i wanted the front of the leather strap to be as wide as where it attaches to the back, this 3D armrest design would not do.

After thinking for some time, I drew a mirror image of the cabriole leg, and also tried ways of making the shape stronger. After some google reasearch of archetypical classic design shapes, I quickly realized what I was aiming for was a Lyre shaped armrest.

Taking inspiration from it,

I added a ball to the top, and presto!

Update 06-04-2016

So i have been very busy the last week.

Lots and lots of exams for school, and of course, the chair!

on the side I secretely experimented with decorative nails ad ways of attaching leather to my wood., for the armrests.

 Next up, was cleaning up  my laminations and sawing My lyre arms.       Glueing the laminations. And then it was time to glue it all together.

posts.title: The making of an escape room puzzle
posts.excerpt: So here is one of my first assignments as a business! And a very interesting enjoyable one at that! Meet the Remington. A piece of mechanical beauty, right? Now as for the assignment, the idea is that someone types in a…
posts.content: So here is one of my first assignments as a business! And a very interesting enjoyable one at that! Meet the Remington.  A piece of mechanical beauty, right? Now as for the assignment, the idea is that someone types in a word, and then a different word is typed on the paper – i.e. the next clue. So I figured, if I could mix the hammers, that would achieve that. After a lot of deliberation, with some complex restraints, such as that no letter could be used twice, I came up with several combinations!   But none really seemed good enough.. Plus, upon closer inspection, I realized, it wasn't going to be quite so easy. The arms all have their own angle, and would make a different place impossible. I considered, sawing them and then re-welding them, but in the end had a better idea. Using 3D printing devices, I would make my own stamps! I was able to open up the bottleneck of the puzzle options!   The trick would be,   WINGS to CLOCK       After a couple of attempts, tinkering with the settings (this here is 3mmx2mm), with 3D-printing I was able make my own hammers!   So went home, got the angle grinder out, and removed the original stamp off the typewriter hammers.   Here I was getting excited as I had the first letter "C" working. The stamps on the right are the ones I hadn't added yet, and are still ground flat. Not satisfied with the level of accuracy of the stamps, i set to cleaning them. Coming up to a better, end result, the letters are defined and well pressed, the hammers i really tested, and seemed to have no problem with any level of intensity in typing. I am afraid the only picture I have the typeset is a little off, the O hasn't really claimed its space. This is down to my ineptitude of typing, wherein you really need to fully press the key, before it moves your page up a little. But the overall project has definitely been a successful one, and the escape room I built it for, they where mighty impressed!

posts.title: Designing a chair
posts.excerpt: INSPIRATIONAL PHASE I have always been drawn to the personification of chairs. I adore the feeling of an object, seemingly coming to life. "A chair's function is not just to provide a place to sit; it is to provide a…
posts.content:
INSPIRATIONAL PHASE

I have always been drawn to the personification of chairs.

I adore the feeling of an object, seemingly coming to life.

"A chair's function is not just to provide a place to sit; it is to provide a medium for self-expression. Chairs are about status, for example. Or signalling something about oneself. That's why the words chair, seat and bench have found themselves used to describe high status professions, from academia to Parliament to the law."

Evan Davis

After much deliberation, I decided to settle for a chair which I found both relatively simple and talkative.

The legs are positioned in a way that makes it seem ready to pounce.

The back panel has an appealing, delicious softness to it, reminiscent of lilies and elephant ears.

SKETCH PHASE

So I sketched out my own version as a first step (see above). But immediately then I ran into trouble as the back to seat connection is illogical from an engineering woodworker's perspective.

DEFINITIVE DESIGN

I thought long and hard about how I could address this, and figured, if I use a sandwich construction for the seat connection, that might work. And a dovetail connection for the back, it might be enough to bear the load.

    But I still wasn't completely satisfied. Then it hit me,

 I would need to translate the forces laterally.

The diagram drawn under here explains this.

 

Then I had yet another idea - what if I gave it a rolling bar?

This relieves a lot of tension from the front connection.

 So my internal engineer came up with this:

posts.title: a Taleidoscope (Beatific Viewer)
posts.excerpt: MARTERIALENMIX Here is a link to my material research, including bending bamboo, and soft robotics. After a lot of delibiration, we came to a plan that deviated a lot from the research, but fitted the study better.…
posts.content:
MARTERIALENMIX

Here is a link to my material research, including bending bamboo, and soft robotics.

After a lot of delibiration, we came to a plan that deviated a lot from the research, but fitted the study better.

materialenmix onderzoek

The sketches, and plan

The idea is to use angled mirrors, at an even part of 360 degrees, to emulate a taleidoscopic effect.

Yes, Taleidoscopic, not Kaleidoscopic.

The difference lies, in the fact that kalei, comes from the ancient greek for beads, which you view through these two mirrors, as opposed to Taleidocope, which doesnt have the beads.

The two mirrors, are looked alongside the surface, and therefore get the chance to endlessly reflect in themselves.

17-9-2015 kaleido front

The execution

Polishing the copper 

    

 

I couldn't resist trying a little etching, seen as I was using etching plates to begin with...

The glueing process was quite complex, as the sides arent parallel.

for the wedges i split my original design in two, as to have a variable depth.

For the glueing of the two symetrical parts, I used gravity to my advantage.

Finally, i redid my sawed fronts.

This time in copper!

To be continued!

next time, I will be folding the metal, and making screwholes, and inserting the screws!

       

Cutting off the ends with a chisel..

I have some pics of the finished product here, will be adding more later.

What still needs to be done for next time:

install glass window,

adjust screws on the side,

Rethink wedge system, it worked, but can be smarter..

posts.title: NEWS
RYAN REDDY
posts.excerpt: Ryan van Lil-Reddy, born to Geraldine M. Reddy and Ton van Lil, (respectively a communications management senior and a manager of building engineering in the centre of Amsterdam) in Amsterdam 21-09-1991. They are just…
posts.content: Ryan van Lil-Reddy, born to Geraldine M. Reddy and Ton van Lil, (respectively a communications management senior and a manager of building engineering in the centre of Amsterdam) in Amsterdam 21-09-1991. They are just the start in a long line of artisans and engineers that came before to become me, among which my grandfathers, a steel-engineer/architect, and a carpenter. Further down the line a tailor and a cigar maker. All the way back to my great-great-great-grandfather Albertus Hendrikus van Lil owning and running one of the first paper mills, in Apeldoorn back in 1504. I have long searched for what I want to do to make this world a better place, I have attempted direct sales for good causes, journalism, management, I've been a chef, sidestepped into modelling and acting You can check my linked-in for more. Alan Watts once inspired me to just go and do what really makes me happy. And to do it so much, I could get really really good at it. And here I am. Paris 2016
